title: StoryHearth – Personalised storybooks starring your family
page_key: 127.0.0.1:8765/ | Your family's stories, bound for generations.

output.observation: The StoryHearth home page introduces a service that turns family memories into personalised illustrated storybooks. It offers “Log in” and a prominent “Proceed” button, explains a three-step process, and states that a digital preview is free while printed hardcovers are shipped across the UK.
output.think_aloud: This sounds very relevant, and the three steps are easy to understand. But that first explanatory paragraph is full of “multimodal generative narrative engine” and “lived-experience corpus”—that’s workshop language nobody would use with a four-year-old. The grey text is hard to read too.

site_model.what_it_is: A website for making personalised illustrated family storybooks from supplied family memories.
site_model.who_it_is_for: Families wanting stories featuring their children and other family members or pets.
site_model.value_proposition: Turn a family memory into an illustrated book, with a free digital preview and an optional printed hardcover.
main_tasks: Add a child and another character
Describe a memory, treasured object, and place
Generate and read a storybook preview
Check and order a printed hardcover
site_model.pricing_model: A free digital preview is advertised; printed hardcovers are available, but no price is shown on this page.
trust_signals: A three-step explanation of how the service works
A named company and contact details appear in the footer, though I cannot read them clearly
site_model.fit_for_me: It could help me make a book about Conker for Lily and read it with her, but I need clearer, plainer wording and more readable text.

page_review.purpose: Explain the service and let me start creating a story, log in, or view pricing.
page_review.what_is_happening: I have arrived at the public home page. The service description, two main calls to action, a three-step explanation, customer quotations, and frequently asked questions are visible at different scroll positions.
page_review.first_impression: The heading and big buttons are clear enough, but the main description uses ridiculous jargon and much of the supporting writing is pale and difficult for my eyes.

walkthrough.q1_would_try: Yes, once I get past the need to log in; this is the service my friend mentioned.
walkthrough.q2_notice_control: Yes, the dark “Log in” button is prominent at the top right, and the orange “Proceed” button is also visible.
walkthrough.q3_label_matches_goal: “Log in” is clear for signing into my account, while “Proceed” is less explicit but reasonable once I know I am starting a story.

issues.title: The opening explanation is written in needlessly technical language
issues.evidence: “Leverage our multimodal generative narrative engine to synthesise bespoke, heirloom-grade story artefacts from your household's lived-experience corpus.”
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: I have to work out what it means, and I cannot make a proper judgement of the service from those words.
issues.fix: Replace it with plain language, such as: “Turn a special family memory into a personalised illustrated storybook featuring your own family.”

issues.title: Supporting text has weak contrast
issues.evidence: “Leverage our multimodal generative narrative engine…” and “Free digital preview · Printed hardcovers shipped across the UK” are shown in pale grey or beige.
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: I can see the large heading, but the smaller supporting text is difficult to read even at 200% zoom.
issues.fix: Use near-black body text on white or another strongly contrasting background, and maintain at least WCAG AA contrast.

issues.title: Main image has no useful description
issues.evidence: [image (no description) 577x440]
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: I cannot tell whether it shows an example storybook or is only decoration.
issues.fix: Give the image meaningful alternative text, or mark it decorative if it conveys no information.

issues.title: Primary action is vague
issues.evidence: [5] link "Proceed →"
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: I am not told whether I will be taken to a form, a login, or the first creation step.
issues.fix: Label the button “Create your storybook” and explain that I will be asked a few simple questions.

issues.title: Footer text is too faint and small to read
issues.evidence: Some text is too faint, including “Privacy”, “Terms”, “Contact”, and “© 2026 StoryHearth Ltd.”
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: I cannot check the company details, privacy information, terms, or contact route.
issues.fix: Use larger, dark, high-contrast footer text and descriptive labels for every link.

positives: The large heading clearly states that this is about family stories.
The three-step explanation is broken into plain, understandable stages below the jargon.
The “Log in” button is prominent and clearly labelled.
The page says the digital preview is free and delivery is available across the UK.

output.memory_note: The home page says the digital preview is free, but gives no printed-book price yet.
output.plan: I shall click the clearly labelled “Log in” button and use the account details provided, rather than start with the less explicit “Proceed” button.

title: Log in – StoryHearth

output.observation: The StoryHearth login page is open, with a 'Welcome back' form containing email and password fields, a large 'Log in' button, and a link to create an account. At 200% zoom, only part of the page is visible, while the footer text below is faint and unreadable.
output.think_aloud: Well, this looks straightforward enough. I can see the email box, password box and a big Log in button, though the boxes rely on pale placeholder writing rather than proper labels. I have my account details, so I'll fill them in carefully and sign in.
output.last_action_feedback: yes — the new page title and heading changed to 'Log in' and 'Welcome back', clearly showing that my click worked.

page_review.purpose: Let an existing StoryHearth customer sign in to create and use a family storybook.
page_review.what_is_happening: The page presents two empty sign-in fields and a large Log in button, with a link for people creating an account. The privacy, terms, contact, and copyright links are below the visible area.
page_review.first_impression: The main login job is clear and the button is large, but the pale placeholder text is difficult for my eyes. I feel more confident once I look at the overall arrangement rather than reading every faint detail.

walkthrough.q1_would_try: Yes, this is exactly what I expected the Log in link to do.
walkthrough.q2_notice_control: Yes, the two large fields and the orange 'Log in' button are easy to notice.
walkthrough.q3_label_matches_goal: The button clearly says 'Log in', and the placeholders 'Email' and 'Password' tell me what to put in them, though permanent field labels would be better.

issues.title: Login fields are not visibly labelled
issues.evidence: [5] textbox (no label) placeholder "Email"; [6] textbox (no label) placeholder "Password"
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: The pale placeholder writing may disappear or be hard to read at 200% zoom, and placeholders are not a dependable label.
issues.fix: Put permanent, high-contrast labels such as 'Email address' above the fields, and keep visible text inside each field when something is typed.

issues.title: Footer links are too faint and small
issues.evidence: Privacy; Terms; Contact; and © 2026 StoryHearth Ltd. are marked faint/small text I cannot make out
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: I cannot read the privacy, terms, or contact information, which makes the site feel less trustworthy.
issues.fix: Use darker, larger footer text with a contrast ratio that remains readable at 200% zoom.

positives: The 'Welcome back' heading is large and reassuring.
The orange 'Log in' button is large, clearly named, and easy to see.
The email and password boxes are large enough to target comfortably.

output.plan: I will enter my email address and password exactly as supplied, then press the clearly labelled Log in button and wait for the next screen.

title: My books – StoryHearth

output.observation: The account dashboard shows a “Welcome back, Demo” heading, says there are no books yet, and offers a prominent “+ Create a new book” button. A message also reports “Error 0x80070057: profile sync incomplete.”
output.think_aloud: I can see the large orange “Create a new book” button clearly enough, which is the right next step. The error message worries me, though—I’m not sure whether my account is properly set up, but the page still lets me carry on.
output.last_action_feedback: partly — the page clearly shows that I logged in because it says “Welcome back, Demo” and offers “Log out,” but the “profile sync incomplete” error makes me unsure whether everything loaded properly.

page_review.purpose: Shows the books in the account and provides a way to create a new book.
page_review.what_is_happening: The account has no existing books, so the page presents “+ Create a new book.” A profile sync error is visible above the welcome message.
page_review.first_impression: The layout is uncluttered and the main button is easy to spot. I’m put off by the error code, which looks more like a workshop error message than a helpful explanation.

walkthrough.q1_would_try: Yes, I would try creating the book because that is exactly what I came here to do.
walkthrough.q2_notice_control: Yes, the large orange “+ Create a new book” button stands out.
walkthrough.q3_label_matches_goal: Yes. “Create a new book” plainly tells me it will start a book.

issues.title: Error message gives no useful explanation or recovery
issues.evidence: “Error 0x80070057: profile sync incomplete.”
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: I worry that I may have done something wrong, and I cannot tell whether the problem will affect my book.
issues.fix: Replace the code with plain wording such as “Some of your profile details have not loaded. You can continue, but your book may not include them,” and provide a clear “Try again” or “Continue without profile details” button.

issues.title: Profile sync failure is presented without reassurance
issues.evidence: “Error 0x80070057: profile sync incomplete.”
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: I am left wondering whether the account is still safe to use or whether the book will be incomplete.
issues.fix: Show whether the account is usable and explain the next step, rather than displaying only a technical error.

issues.title: Footer text is too faint to read
issues.evidence: The visible notes say “Privacy”, “Terms”, “Contact”, and “© 2026 StoryHearth Ltd.” are faint/small and cannot be read.
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: I need to be able to check the privacy and contact information if I am unsure about the service.
issues.fix: Use darker, larger text and larger link targets for the footer.

positives: The “+ Create a new book” button is large, clearly labelled, and easy to notice.
The page says plainly that there are no books yet, so I know I am not overlooking something.
The main navigation labels are written in ordinary language.

output.memory_note: The dashboard showed a profile sync error, but the account still appeared to allow book creation.
output.plan: I will click “+ Create a new book” and see what information the site needs before I begin the story.

title: Create your book – StoryHearth

output.observation: The screen asks me to choose the book's reading level and illustration style before continuing. “Lexile 200L–500L” and “Watercolour — soft and dreamy” are currently selected.
output.think_aloud: Well, it has saved my story and brought me to the look-and-feel choices. “Lexile 200L–500L” sounds like workshop jargon to me, but since Lily is only four, the site seems to have made that choice for her; the watercolour picture also sounds lovely.
output.last_action_feedback: partly — the next page appeared, so the Next button worked, but nothing reminded me that the last part of my 300-character memory had been cut off at 200 characters.

page_review.purpose: Choose the reading difficulty and visual style for Lily's personalised book.
page_review.what_is_happening: The page presents four reading-level radio buttons and three illustration-style radio buttons. The middle reading level and watercolour style are selected, with Back and Next controls below.
page_review.first_impression: This is fairly straightforward and the large choices are easy to see. Lexile is not a word I know, though, so I need to rely on the sensible default that has already been ticked for a four-year-old.

walkthrough.q1_would_try: Yes, I would accept the reading level and choose an illustration style.
walkthrough.q2_notice_control: Yes, the clearly labelled illustration radio buttons are visible after scrolling, although the first two controls are off-screen at my current zoom.
walkthrough.q3_label_matches_goal: Partly. The illustration labels match my choice well, but the Lexile labels do not plainly explain which level is best for a four-year-old.

issues.title: Reading-level choices use unexplained jargon
issues.evidence: The heading is “Reading level”, followed only by “Lexile BR–200L”, “Lexile 200L–500L”, “Lexile 500L–800L”, and “Lexile 800L+”.
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: I cannot confidently judge these labels for a four-year-old, so I may choose the wrong level and make the book too hard or too babyish.
issues.fix: Give each option a plain-English age description, such as “Age 4–6 — Lily can read independently” or “Age 6–8 — Lily and an adult can read together”, with Lexile details shown as secondary information.

issues.title: The preselected reading level is not explained
issues.evidence: “Lexile 200L–500L” is checked without any visible explanation of why that was selected.
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: I can see the selection, but I do not know whether the site chose it because Lily is four or merely selected the middle option.
issues.fix: State plainly, for example, “Recommended for a 4-year-old, based on the age you entered”.

issues.title: Footer links are effectively invisible at this zoom
issues.evidence: The links labelled with faint, unreadable text lead to “/privacy.html”, “/privacy.html#terms”, and “mailto:hello@storyhearth.test”.
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: I cannot find the privacy, terms, or contact information, which makes me less comfortable trusting the site with family memories.
issues.fix: Use dark, high-contrast text at a readable size, and enlarge the click targets to at least 44 by 44 pixels.

positives: The page heading and group labels are large and readable.
